title: She Wouldn't Jump.
description:
The first victim of the Great Fire of London was a young woman whose name was never recorded. She worked in Thomas Farriner's bakery on Pudding Lane.

In the early hours of 2 September 1666, she would not jump from the upstairs window. She became the first of six recorded deaths in a fire that destroyed four-fifths of the City of London over the next four days — thirteen thousand two hundred houses, eighty-seven parish churches, Old St Paul's Cathedral, about a hundred thousand Londoners made homeless.

The Monument to the Great Fire stands 202 feet tall, 202 feet from where the bakery stood. It bears the names of the kings, the architects, and the city officials who built it. It does not bear hers.

Recreated from the household accounts, the British Library letter of October 1666, and the parliamentary investigation that followed.
